digest.component_or_area: Review gate discovery and policy architecture
propositions: Plan review and code review currently use partially independent registry, routing, runner, checkpoint, and failure paths leading to policy-ownership defects where one gate can disable built-ins, omit activated criteria, ignore applicability, or mistake failed work for success.

A unified review-discovery architecture must route both gates through one immutable repository-bound effective-policy snapshot containing built-ins, project LLM criteria, project DET criteria, routing, and posture, with gate-owned strategies retaining context and a shared executor handling typed outcomes, budget enforcement, and success-only checkpoints.

Project code-review LLM criteria require non-empty repository-relative globs; project.review-phase-boundaries must migrate from empty list to ["**"] preserving membership and eliminating stale documentation referencing the old empty-list semantics.

The shared discovery executor must emit typed success, resumed, skipped, shed, failed, and cancelled outcomes; only success and resumed outcomes may seed the new checkpoint namespace, and the failure policy must skip dependency-blocked work and return unsigned INDETERMINATE when blocking coverage is missing unless a real blocking finding takes precedence.

Code review must preserve sequential execution, no checkpoints, base-reviewer payloads, and authored YAML/BPMN topology; plan review must preserve chunking, concurrency, cache warming, and cancellation behavior while moving to digest-complete checkpoints in a new namespace.

The rebar review-plan --retry command must reuse content-identical successes, retry only missing calls with fresh budget, refuse stale/ineligible lineage before any model call, and be documented in CLI help, generated reference, user guide, plan-review guide, and exit-code guidance.
